chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Hammad ibn Isa from Hariz from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:

I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about a Muslim who slaughtered an animal and mentioned the name of God, but the blade preceded his intention, thus exposing the head, and he said: 'If the blood flows out, eat it.'

key_terms.فَسَبَقَتْهُ حَدِيدَةٌ: the blade preceded him (moved before the cut was completed/intended)

ai.seo_question: Is an animal halal if the slaughterer's blade moved before the intention was fully formed?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Baqir (AS), the criterion for valid slaughter is shifted from the precision of the incision to the presence of blood flow, emphasizing the practical reality of the act over ritual perfection. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle of ease (yusr) in dietary laws, where the essential conditions of Islam and tasmiyah are met, and the physical sign of slaughter (blood) is present, rendering the meat halal despite minor mechanical imperfections.
